title: Plant Scheduling Rule: Counting a Late Acknowledgment Into the Ship Date (Factory Production Orders)
content:
For Factory Production Orders, the ship date revised for a late order acknowledgment is fixed as follows.

**Return window.** The return window closes on the last of the class acknowledgment return business days, counted starting the day after the order entry date, Monday through Friday excluding U.S. federal holidays.

**Late-acknowledgment shift.** The late-acknowledgment shift is the business days of signature lateness, counted from the day after the return window closes up to and including the date the acknowledgment was signed.

**Revised ship date.** The late-acknowledgment revised ship date is the current ship date moved later by the late-acknowledgment shift, counted in business days starting the day after the current ship date.

**Figure recorded.** The figure recorded with the late-acknowledgment notice is the late-acknowledgment revised ship date written as the number of calendar days from the handling date to that date.

## Records each quantity is read from

| Quantity | Record |
|---|---|
| order entry date | the factory order record |
| return window length | the class acknowledgment return business days |
| signature date | the acknowledgment signed checkpoint on the order's milestone records |
| current ship date | the factory order record, as it stands on the handling date |
| handling date | the date the notice is recorded |

## Worked example (hypothetical dates, no federal holiday in the period)

- An order is entered on a Monday; its return window is 3 business days. The window runs Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday and closes on the Thursday.
- The acknowledgment is signed on the Wednesday of the following week. Counting from the Friday after the window closed up to and including that Wednesday gives Friday, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday: a shift of 4 business days.
- The order's current ship date is a Friday. Moving it 4 business days later, counting from the following Monday, reaches the Thursday six calendar days after it.
- The notice is recorded on the Monday eleven calendar days before that current ship date. From that Monday to the revised Thursday is 17 calendar days, so the figure recorded is 17.

## Points of reading

- Only business days count toward the shift; Saturdays, Sundays and U.S. federal holidays are skipped both in the lateness count and when the current ship date is moved.
- The figure recorded is in calendar days, measured from the handling date, not from the current ship date.
